title: Safe small Markdown to HTML converter
when: An app must render user written Markdown (notes, comments, a preview pane) as HTML without external libraries.
prompt:
Goal: A small converter for a documented Markdown subset that escapes all input first, so user text cannot inject HTML or scripts.
Steps:
1. Escape &, <, >, double and single quotes in the whole input before any transform; only the converter produces markup.
2. Blocks line by line: fenced code (kept escaped until the closing fence), # to ###### headings, - and 1. lists, > quotes, rules, blank line paragraphs.
3. Inline rules on non code text in order: code spans first (protected), then **bold**, *italic*, [text](url).
4. Links: allow http:, https:, mailto: and relative URLs only; drop javascript: and data:; add rel="noopener" to external links.
5. Document the subset; unsupported syntax stays plain text.
6. Insert through DOMParser keeping only allowed tags and attributes, and test hostile input (<script>, onerror, javascript: links, unclosed fences).
Quality bar:
- Output is balanced HTML.
- A 50 KB note converts in milliseconds.
- Lists and line breaks behave as users expect.
Pitfalls:
- Escaping after converting, which lets raw HTML through.
- Nested emphasis regexes that hang on long lines.
- Raw HTML passthrough "for flexibility".
Verify:
- [ ] Escaping happens first.
- [ ] Link scheme allow list.
- [ ] Hostile input tests pass.
- [ ] No eval.
Output: js/markdown.js exporting toHTML(markdown), and tests with hostile cases.

examples.input: preview de markdown nas anotações sem biblioteca
examples.output: toHTML escaping first, headings, lists, code fences, bold, italic, safe links, tests with <script>
